name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.149.0 — Reopening an addressed client request now leaves the row in the exact shape a server render would produce: the accept/reopen pair, the why textarea (cleared) and the See-journey link all hide, the withdraw control (rendered hidden on every addressed article) reveals, and the reopen answers in the shared msg slot with the same saved receipt the ask form uses. The row also remembers a second round — an open request whose thread carries a client reopen reads 'We'll look at this again' and shows a 'You said: ...' line with the latest text, rendered identically by the server and by the client-side handler so a reload never erases the client's own words. 7.148.0 — The client player becomes a loop the client drives, and its two pages become a designed surface. A journey's state is derived from the client's own requests (unseen | walking | changes-requested | fixed | ok | waived, lib/mocks-walk.js journeyState) rather than stored: an open request outranks a stale confirmation, a request on an OK'd journey takes the confirmation back into history, and the confirm route refuses until nothing is open or awaiting the client's check. The client accepts (Looks good) or reopens (Still not right, with their own words) an addressed request, and takes back an open one with Never mind — without that control a client who changed their mind locked the journey until a seven-day timeout. A journey is listed when its page exists, never when a session flag says so, so redrawing one no longer takes it away from the client who already approved it. The index is now the product rather than a ticket queue: one card per journey whose hero is a four-slot rail of its own screens rendered as the real mocks scaled down, a dot on the screen carrying a request, one action whose verb follows the state, and the request log below. The player is two zones — screens as a step indicator in the bar, the mock framed under its caption — and confirming is the last step of the walk. The CLIENT step prints whether the server answers, each journey's state, and what the client left with the one command per item; the server is the user's own long-lived process. 7.147.0 — spec-review-driver.js refuses a --mark against a spec copy that carries no review sidecar instead of answering it with the terminal cold-path DONE. A mark issued from the main root after a worktree merge landed (status already done, sidecar still in the worktree) exited 0 without dispatching the mark, so finishMerge() never ran: evidence was never promoted and the worktree was never cleaned up, stranding the build and review ledger rows inside a worktree that was then deleted. The refusal names the linked-worktree copy of the spec that owns the sidecar and prints the corrected re-run command; bare and --state invocations still answer DONE.
